Verbal

solution.paragraph: A sequence where each successive term of the sequence increases (or decreases) by a constant value.

problem.paragraph: How is the common difference of an arithmetic sequence found?
How do we determine whether a sequence is arithmetic?

solution.paragraph: We find whether the difference between all consecutive terms is the same. This is the same as saying that the sequence has a common difference.

problem.paragraph: What are the main differences between using a recursive formula and using an explicit formula to describe an arithmetic sequence?
Describe how linear functions and arithmetic sequences are similar. How are they different?

solution.paragraph: Both arithmetic sequences and linear functions have a constant rate of change. They are different because their domains are not the same; linear functions are defined for all real numbers, and arithmetic sequences are defined for natural numbers or a subset of the natural numbers.
